question.text: 'Suryavanshi Capital AIF' (a trust) is launching its third scheme. The sponsor asks the manager whether a fresh Investment Management Agreement (IMA) must be signed for this new scheme. What is the correct position?

answer.text: The IMA is signed once for the trust as a whole and not at the launch of each scheme
A fresh IMA must be signed for every new scheme launched under the AIF
IMA is only required for Category III AIFs, not Category I/II
IMA must be renewed every 5 years irrespective of scheme launches

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 13.3, the IMA is signed once for the trust as a whole and is not signed at the launch of each scheme. The trustee delegates management powers to the investment manager via this single agreement, except for certain retained powers identified in the Indenture of Trust. **The Trap:** Fresh IMA per scheme is a common misconception — the IMA operates at trust level, while each scheme has its own PPM and Contribution Agreements. IMA applies to all AIF categories. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B cover that IMA exists; XIX-C Manager exam tests nuances like one-time execution, retained trustee powers, and termination mechanics. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When negotiating the IMA at trust inception, bake in enough scope flexibility to cover future schemes — amending IMA later may trigger trustee consent and potentially LP material-change rights.
